question: For the next MLIP round starting from the current remote-derived base_unit under the fixed benchmark contract, what evidence-backed exploit angles and next-phase jump angles are justified now?

notes: model.py uses all-pairs distances within a hard cutoff, concatenates atom embeddings and Gaussian RBF features, and sums pair energies.
No graph neighborhood updates, no directional features, and no explicit periodic/cell handling are present.
train.py optimizes L1 energy plus weighted L1 force loss on per-sample autograd forces.
eval.py targets rMD17 and ISO17 only, with anchored Q score computed from mixed force and energy MAE.

recent_briefs_checked.warning: Contained no verified paper or repo evidence, so not relied on for claims.

strong_papers.title: High-performance training and inference for deep equivariant interatomic potentials
strong_papers.local_pdf: /mnt/c/Users/1/Desktop/文献/MLIP/MLIP等变训练 - NequIP高性能训练推理深度等变原子间势.pdf
signals: Deep equivariant models improve data efficiency, generalization, and state-of-the-art accuracy in MLIP simulations.
Framework supports compiled training/inference, dynamic tensor shapes, and distributed training.
Allegro models trained on SPICE 2 used 6.0 Å cutoff and tensor-product equivariant features, with substantial inference speedups after compilation.
strong_papers.relevance: Supports justified jump from pair-only invariant model to local equivariant message passing, while highlighting implementation complexity and deployment cost.

strong_papers.title: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry
strong_papers.local_pdf: /mnt/c/Users/1/Desktop/文献/MLIP/MLIP基础模型 - MACE-MP原子材料化学基础模型.pdf
signals: MACE unifies ACE-style body-order expansion with equivariant graph neural networks.
Authors emphasize stable molecular dynamics, broad transfer, and fine-tuning from foundation initialization on small task-specific data.
Higher-order equivariant message passing is treated as the key modeling ingredient beyond simpler local models.
strong_papers.relevance: Supports next-phase jump toward higher-order equivariant message passing; also suggests exploit path via injecting higher-body structure before full foundation-scale complexity.

strong_papers.title: Machine learning of charges and long-range interactions from energies and forces
strong_papers.local_pdf: /mnt/c/Users/1/Desktop/文献/MLIP/MLIP长程相互作用 - 从能量和力学习电荷与长程作用.pdf
signals: LES splits energy into short-range and long-range parts and predicts latent charges from local features without supervising explicit charges.
LES can be combined with short-range MLIPs including ACE, GAP, MTP, NequIP, and MACE.
Long-range augmentation helps strongly electrostatic or charged systems and can outperform explicit charge-learning baselines.
strong_papers.relevance: Interesting next-phase direction, but current fixed benchmark targets rMD17 and ISO17 where missing angular/message structure is the more immediate gap than long-range electrostatics.

strong_papers.title: Online test-time adaptation for better generalization of interatomic potentials to out-of-distribution data
strong_papers.local_pdf: /mnt/c/Users/1/Desktop/文献/MLIP/MLIP泛化 - TAIP在线测试时适应分布外数据.pdf
signals: TAIP adds dual-level self-supervised adaptation during inference, reducing energy and force errors on MD17, ISO17, water, and electrolyte benchmarks without extra training data.
Reported average force/energy improvements are roughly 30 to 40 percent across several OOD settings.
Method requires an encoder-based MLIP with self-supervised heads and test-time parameter updates.
strong_papers.relevance: Benchmark-relevant in principle because it directly improves MD17/ISO17 OOD generalization, but implementation fit to the current minimalist model is poor and risks violating benchmark simplicity/runtime expectations.

Multiple interaction layers with tensor-product message passing
Autograd derivatives for forces and compiled training/inference

Optional pair repulsion and multiple domain heads

strong_repos.fit_notes: Useful evidence for a structured exploit path adding angular/body-order information and optional long-range modules, but still a large step from current code.

exploit_angles.angle: Add lightweight local message passing over cutoff neighbors while keeping scalar invariant outputs and autograd forces.
justification: Current base_unit already builds neighbor-like pair features from atom embeddings plus RBF distances, so edge aggregation is the smallest structural extension.
Verified NequIP and MACE repo evidence shows interaction layers are the core mechanism for improving local-environment modeling.
Verified local NequIP/MACE papers support the claim that richer local interactions, not just optimizer tweaks, drive better accuracy and generalization.

exploit_angles.angle: Inject directional or three-body structure before full equivariance, for example angular basis or triplet features on top of current distance features.
justification: Current model is strictly pairwise within cutoff, which is a sharp capability gap for directional chemistry and conformational OOD behavior on rMD17/ISO17.
MACE paper and CACE repo both verify the importance of higher-body structural representations beyond plain pair pooling.
This is a balanced exploit because it can preserve simple scalar training/eval plumbing while addressing the most obvious missing inductive bias.

exploit_angles.angle: Keep the same benchmark loss shape but improve parameterization of the local model, for example deeper edge MLP plus neighbor aggregation rather than isolated pair scoring.
justification: Base unit loss/eval stack is already benchmark-compatible and simple.
Evidence points to architectural locality upgrades as more justified than pure training-hyperparameter search.

jump_angles.angle: Jump to a minimal E(3)-equivariant local model in the NequIP/MACE family.
justification: Verified local paper evidence from NequIP and MACE supports equivariant models as a major accuracy/generalization phase transition for MLIPs.
Verified repo evidence confirms practical implementations rely on spherical harmonics, tensor products, and multi-layer interaction blocks.

jump_angles.angle: Explore a CACE-style higher-body Cartesian expansion path as a bridge between simple pair models and full equivariant GNNs.
justification: Verified repo evidence shows CACE includes angular/product-basis machinery and optional inter-atomic message passing.
This may be a more incremental jump than full irreps-heavy equivariance while still moving beyond pairwise geometry.

jump_angles.angle: Reserve long-range latent-charge augmentation as a later jump, not the first next round default.
justification: Verified LES paper evidence is strong for electrostatic and charged systems, but current benchmark and base-unit capability gap point more strongly to missing local geometry/body-order bias.
Adding long-range machinery now risks complexity without targeting the dominant observed structural deficiency.

jump_angles.angle: Treat TAIP-style test-time adaptation as a research branch rather than the default next-round candidate.
justification: Verified local TAIP paper directly reports gains on MD17 and ISO17-like settings.
But adapting the current model into an encoder plus self-supervised test-time update framework is a poor fit for a single bounded round starting from this base_unit.

best_near_term: deeper local interaction/readout without changing benchmark contract

Foundation-model scale claims from MACE paper should not be interpreted as directly implementable inside the current minimal base_unit without substantial rewrite.
